TIAGO FERRÃO-LINDQVIST
Data Engineering | Test Data Processing & Reporting
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [LOCATION]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Test and Validation Engineer with experience building Python-based tools to process rig data, check test results against specifications and generate reports. Developed a nightly processing workflow handling approximately 2 GB of TDMS and CSV data per week from six rigs, with results written to a staging table in SQL Server. Also built a Power BI dashboard used by validation and design engineers. Bringing hands-on data-processing experience and ongoing data engineering study to a move into data engineering.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data processing: Python scripting, pandas, NumPy, SQL, MATLAB, Simulink
Data and reporting: SQL Server, SQLite, Power BI, Matplotlib, npTDMS
Other tools: Flask, Git, Docker Compose (tutorial-based personal project), Windows Task Scheduler

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components | 2019–Present
- Conduct durability and vibration testing, test-data tooling and root-cause analysis.
- Built Python scripts to parse test-rig TDMS and CSV output, process approximately 2 GB of data per week across six rigs, flag channels outside test specifications and generate report figures.
- Scheduled the processing workflow to run nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler; writes summary results to a staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database, created by IT.
- Packaged the tool for internal use; four other test engineers use it for their own tests.
- Created a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation; used by approximately 15 engineers across validation and design.
- Developed a MATLAB/Simulink model of a seat-adjuster drive, including motor, gearbox and rail friction, to select rig load profiles matching customer duty cycles.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps | 2014–2019
- Designed pump casings and impellers and performed structural finite element analysis (FEA).
- Supported performance test-bench activities.

PROJECTS
Bike-sharing trips API | Personal learning project | 2025
- Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only endpoints.
- Runs locally on a laptop; followed a tutorial to run it with Docker Compose.
- Technologies: Python, Flask, SQLite, Docker Compose, Git.

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Online Data Engineering Course | In progress
- Completed 6 of 9 modules; no certificate awarded to date.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Portuguese citizen (EU). Happy to commute to Lisbon for hybrid work.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, credible, and appropriately honest about the candidate’s level of data-engineering experience. It gives strong quantified evidence: approximately 2 GB of data per week, six rigs, four internal users, and approximately 15 dashboard users. The strongest content is the description of the nightly processing workflow, SQL Server staging-table output, specification checks, and Power BI reporting. The document also makes the transition from test engineering into data engineering understandable. Its main limitation is not poor writing but the substantial senior-level gap between the candidate’s current experience and the role’s expectations. The use of placeholders such as [EMAIL], [PHONE], [LINKEDIN], and [LOCATION] is a professionalism issue if this is the submission version.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, standard reverse-chronological experience, readable bullets, and ATS-friendly plain text formatting. Relevant terms such as Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL, SQL Server, Power BI, data processing, reporting, Docker Compose, Git, Flask, and SQLite are present and supported by the candidate’s information. However, AI and ATS screening for this particular Senior Data Engineer role will likely be low to moderate because the CV does not contain supported evidence of production data platforms, cloud data warehouses, Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, advanced SQL, query optimization, or dimensional modelling. These are genuine experience gaps rather than keyword or formatting defects. Do not add those terms without evidence.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the transferable aspects of the role: building a reusable internal data-processing tool, operating a scheduled workflow, validating data against specifications, writing results to SQL Server, creating reporting for engineering stakeholders, and supporting multiple users. These examples provide some evidence of ownership, practical problem solving, data quality checking, and collaboration with validation and design engineers. The candidate’s ongoing course and personal project also support curiosity and continued development. However, the candidate’s material shows gaps in the central senior requirements: designing and operating production data platforms or cloud warehouses at scale; advanced Python and SQL with query optimization; strong dimensional data modelling; and hands-on cloud experience. The CV shows Portuguese citizenship and states that the candidate is happy to commute to Lisbon for hybrid work, but it does not explicitly establish Portuguese-language proficiency. Overall, this is a credible transferable-skills CV, but it is not a close match for a Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform position.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL: In the contact-information line at the top of the CV, replace [EMAIL], [PHONE], [LINKEDIN], and [LOCATION] with the candidate’s actual professional contact details before submission. Keep the information in a simple single line so it remains ATS-readable.

MINOR: In the Professional Summary section, make the operational and reusable nature of the strongest experience more prominent without implying production-platform or cloud experience. For example, change the opening to: “Test and Validation Engineer who built and operated a scheduled Python data-processing workflow for rig data, validating results against specifications and generating SQL Server-backed reports.” Retain the existing figures and the statement about the ongoing data-engineering course.

MINOR: In the Technical Skills section, add the supported data-quality and workflow terms “test-result validation,” “specification checks,” “scheduled batch processing,” and “technical reporting” under an appropriately named category such as “Data processing and validation.” This makes the candidate’s relevant experience easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without overstating it.

MINOR: In the Corvane Automotive Components experience section, revise the first bullet so the reusable-tool and stakeholder impact appear earlier. For example: “Built and packaged an internal Python data-processing tool now used by four test engineers to process rig output, validate channels against specifications, and generate reports.” This consolidates information already supported elsewhere in the CV and strengthens the ownership and reuse message.

Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Strong data modelling skills (dimensional modelling)
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professionally written, and unusually careful about distinguishing hands-on experience from tutorial-based exposure. The strongest evidence is quantified: approximately 2 GB of data per week, six rigs, four users, and approximately 15 dashboard users. The project descriptions also communicate practical ownership, automation, reporting, and collaboration. However, the document is targeting a Senior Data Engineer – Data Platform role while presenting mainly test-engineering experience, local scripting, and a small personal API project. The seniority and scope of the evidence are therefore substantially below the role's stated expectations. There is also a material inconsistency with the supplied candidate information: the CV says Corvane Automotive Components has been the candidate's employer since 2019, while the supplied original cover letter says the candidate currently works at Halvik Pumps and is applying to Corvane. This must be verified and corrected before submission.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, straightforward chronology, searchable technology names, and conventional bullet formatting. It includes useful terms such as Python, pandas, NumPy, SQL, SQL Server, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, Flask, SQLite, TDMS, and data processing. The document should parse reliably assuming the original formatting does not use columns, graphics, text boxes, headers/footers for essential information, or icons. ATS and AI screening probability for this specific senior platform role is low to moderate because the CV does not truthfully support key matching terms including production data platform, cloud data warehouse, Google Cloud, BigQuery, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, data modelling, query optimisation, or large-scale platform operations. These terms should not be inserted merely for keyword matching because the candidate information explicitly says they are not supported.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV demonstrates relevant adjacent experience: Python-based test-data processing, scheduled workflow operation, SQL Server output, reporting, dashboard development, data-quality checks against specifications, and collaboration with validation and design engineers. These examples can support the company's themes of ownership, practical problem solving, collaboration, and reducing unnecessary manual work. The candidate also states Portuguese citizenship and willingness to commute to Lisbon for hybrid work, which is relevant to the stated location. However, the core senior requirements are not met in the supplied material: production data platforms or cloud warehouses at scale, advanced Python and SQL with query optimisation, strong dimensional data modelling, and hands-on Google Cloud or comparable cloud experience. The candidate also has no stated experience with Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, CI/CD, or production Docker. The CV appropriately avoids falsely claiming these skills. The candidate's curiosity about architecture and open-source practices is only weakly evidenced through the course, personal Git repositories, and a tutorial-based Docker Compose project. Professional English is demonstrated by the quality of the CV itself, but Portuguese-language proficiency is not explicitly documented. Graph modelling is not evidenced.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Experience section, verify the employment chronology against the candidate's authoritative records and correct the conflict between "Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components | 2019–Present" and the supplied original cover letter, which states that the candidate currently works at Halvik Pumps and is applying to Corvane. Do not retain both versions or imply current employment at an employer that is not factually current.

CRITICAL — After correcting the chronology, make the target level more credible without claiming senior platform experience. In the Professional Summary, replace "Bringing hands-on data-processing experience and ongoing data engineering study to a move into data engineering" with a concise statement positioning the candidate as a test and validation engineer transitioning into data engineering through Python data processing, scheduled workflows, SQL Server reporting, and ongoing study. Do not describe the work as a production data platform, cloud data warehouse, advanced SQL, or data modelling because the supplied notes do not support those claims.

MINOR — In the bullet beginning "Built Python scripts," change the wording to make the data-quality function more searchable and precise while preserving the facts. For example: "Built Python scripts using pandas, NumPy and npTDMS to parse TDMS and CSV rig output, process approximately 2 GB of data per week across six rigs, validate channels against test specifications, and generate report figures." 

MINOR — In the workflow bullet, explicitly label the operating environment and limitations so the scope is clear: "Scheduled a nightly workflow on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler; wrote summary results to an IT-created staging table in SQL Server." Do not call this cloud orchestration, platform operations, or database design.

MINOR — In the Professional Experience section under Corvane Automotive Components, strengthen the collaboration and adoption evidence by retaining the concrete user counts in the same bullet or in adjacent bullets: four test engineers use the internal tool, and approximately 15 validation and design engineers use the Power BI dashboard. This is stronger alignment evidence than generic claims about teamwork.

MINOR — In the Technical Skills section, keep Docker Compose explicitly qualified as "tutorial-based personal project" and keep Git limited to personal projects, as currently stated. Do not add Docker, CI/CD, cloud, Airflow, dbt, BigQuery, Spark, Kafka, dimensional modelling, or query optimisation as skills; the candidate's notes explicitly say these are not hands-on capabilities.

MINOR — In the Professional Development section, retain the exact progress statement "Completed 6 of 9 modules; no certificate awarded to date." This is appropriately transparent and prevents the course from being misread as a completed qualification.

Those are candidate-profile gaps rather than writing defects. critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with the data-processing, reporting, Python, SQL Server, dashboard, scheduled-workflow, and cross-functional-use aspects of the role. The CV also does not establish Portuguese-language proficiency, although Portuguese citizenship is stated. The document should position the candidate as a credible transition candidate with practical test-data engineering experience, not as an already-qualified senior data-platform engineer.
